skill.name: socialdatax-media-save-organizer
skill.description: Guides SocialDataX commands to save selected social media images, videos, and audio, with source links, local paths, and download status.
skill.summary: Save media from six supported platforms and organize verified files with their sources.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown backticks, normal API authentication references, documentation links, or readable Chinese text rather than shell substitution, leaked secrets, or obfuscation. Two command locations execute an unpinned npm package through npx, exposing the host and inherited credentials to changing third-party code. No evidence of prompt injection or intentional exfiltration was found; external package implementation was not included for review.

remediation.issue: CLI examples execute socialdatax-skills@latest with automatic npm confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace @latest with a reviewed exact version and lock dependencies. Obtain installation consent and run with minimal filesystem access and credentials.

content.user_title: Save and Organize Social Media Files
content.value_statement: Media from multiple social platforms can lose source context when saved separately. This skill guides SocialDataX downloads and organizes verified paths, source links, and failures.
actual_capabilities: Guides media saving for Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X / Twitter, and Bilibili through SocialDataX commands.
Distinguishes content pages from direct media URLs and selects platform-specific media fields.
Uses separate empty subdirectories for different media items to avoid filename collisions.
Deduplicates repeated media URLs while retaining their source associations.
Records source links, verified local paths, media types, results, and failure reasons.
Checks existing-file status against source records before treating files as already saved.
limitations: The package contains instructions, not a bundled downloader; CLI execution requires Node.js, npm, and the external SocialDataX package.
Online content resolution requires a user-configured SocialDataX API key and may require account credits.
Bilibili merging requires ffmpeg; its listed MCP tool returns download links rather than saving files.
Support is limited to documented platforms and available media; private or missing content and failed downloads are not guaranteed.

use_cases.title: Collect campaign assets
use_cases.description: Save selected campaign media from supplied links and retain sources alongside verified local file paths.

use_cases.title: Build a research collection
use_cases.description: Organize explicitly selected public media and record missing items without inventing download results.

use_cases.title: Resume an editing collection
use_cases.description: Compare an existing source manifest with local files, reuse matching assets, and isolate new downloads.

prompt_templates.title: Save one media file
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this direct media URL: [media URL]. Use [output directory] and report the verified local path or the actual failure.

prompt_templates.title: Collect selected post media
prompt_templates.prompt: Save only the images from these supported-platform posts: [links]. Use [output directory], separate distinct assets, and list their sources and results.

prompt_templates.title: Save a Bilibili video
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this Bilibili video: [video link], into [output directory]. Check required dependencies and request approval before installation. Verify the final file.

prompt_templates.title: Resume and reconcile a collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume these links: [links], using [existing manifest] in [output directory]. Verify existing source mappings, deduplicate media, and report saved, existing, and failed items.

output_examples.input: Save selected images from two posts into my collection directory.
output: Illustrative result: Two distinct images were verified in separate material subdirectories.
Each entry lists its supplied source link, actual local path, image type, and saved status.
The same media URL appeared in both posts; one file was retained with both sources.

output_examples.input: Resume a collection that includes an existing image and an unavailable video.
output: Illustrative result: The existing image matched its source manifest and was marked already present.
The unavailable video was marked failed with the reported download error.
Verified files were retained; no path or successful download was claimed for the failed item.

best_practices: Provide an explicit link list, output directory, and desired media types before execution.
Review the external package version and authorize dependency changes before running downloads.
Verify local files and source mappings, use separate empty subdirectories, and keep credentials out of manifests.
anti_patterns: Do not pass content-page URLs to direct-media download commands.
Do not treat command submission or an unmatched existing file as a successful download.
Do not download extra assets, overwrite unrelated files, or change system configuration without authorization.

faq.question: Which platforms are documented?
faq.answer: Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X / Twitter, and Bilibili are documented. Other platforms are not promised.

faq.question: Do all downloads require an API key?
faq.answer: Direct-media download commands do not require a key. Online detail resolution and Bilibili link requests use SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: CLI execution requires Node.js, npm, and the external SocialDataX package. Bilibili merging also requires ffmpeg.

faq.question: How are duplicate media URLs handled?
faq.answer: The workflow saves each repeated media URL once and retains its source associations. Existing files require a matching source record.

faq.question: What happens when a download fails?
faq.answer: Verified files are retained and failed items include their reported reasons. Insufficient-balance responses stop automatic retries.

faq.question: Does the skill log into social accounts?
faq.answer: The documented workflow does not read browser login data, post content, or interact with social accounts. It saves requested media locally.
